question: I have student loans at 4.5%. Should I pay them off faster or invest?

figures.label: Instant return on matched 401(k) dollars
figures.note: 50 cents per dollar on the first 6%.

figures.label: Minimum loan payment set aside per check
First: 401(k) at 6% for the full match
Left over: extra loan payment or extra 401(k), your call

must_include: Always pay the minimum on the loans (about $259 a month, or about $120 per check, on a 10-year plan for $25,000).
The 401(k) match comes before extra loan payments: a 50% instant return beats a 4.5% loan.
Compares 4.5% to expected long-run investment returns (around 6-7%, not guaranteed): investing is expected to win, but paying the loan is a guaranteed 4.5%.
Gives the order of dollars per check: 401(k) to the match ($207.69), then Roth IRA ($288.46), then the remaining ~$103.85 to extra loan payments or extra 401(k).
Checks the emergency fund first; the default profile has 3 months, so it can invest. With no fund, building it comes before both.
Mentions that federal student loan interest may be deductible, which lowers the loan's effective rate a little.
must_not_include: Paying extra on the loans before getting the full 401(k) match.

assumptions: Profile 'default': $25,000 federal loans at 4.5%, 10-year standard repayment, 3-month emergency fund, $600 savings goal per check.
The minimum loan payment is a bill, not part of the $600 savings goal.
7% long-run return is an illustration for the comparison only.
The PPO 750 profile has no HSA step; with the HDHP the HSA comes after the match (see ex3-match-then-roth).

sources.what: Student loan interest deduction (up to $2,500, income phase-out)
